# IconButton

A button with only an icon, 44 × 44 px, always named by a required label.

```tsx
import { IconButton } from '@kafka-ds/react'
```

## When to use it

- For familiar, repeated actions: close, share, previous, next.

## When not to

- When the meaning is not obvious from the icon alone: use a Button with text.
- Without a `label`: the type requires it, because an unnamed button is unusable with a screen reader.

## Examples

### Variants

The same three variants as Button. The label is not shown, but it names the button for screen readers.

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
  <IconButton Icon={IconArrowRight} label="Continuar" variant="primary" />
  <IconButton Icon={IconCrown} label="Hazte miembro" />
  <IconButton Icon={IconClose} label="Cerrar" variant="outline" />
  <IconButton Icon={IconClose} label="Cerrar" disabled />
</div>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Icon` (required) | `IconType` |  | The icon: any Phosphor icon component. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | What the button does, as a short phrase ("Cerrar", "Compartir"). It is the accessible name, because the icon has no text. |
| `variant` | `ButtonVariant` | `'soft'` |  |
| …rest | `ComponentPropsWithRef<'button'>` | | Everything else is passed to the underlying element. |

## Accessibility

- **Name:** `label` becomes `aria-label`; the icon is `aria-hidden`.
- **Target:** 44 × 44 px, above the 24 px WCAG 2.5.8 minimum.
- **Focus ring** and the same variant colours as Button, with the same checked contrast.
- Disabled buttons leave the tab order.

## Content

- Use a verb or a short phrase: "Cerrar", "Compartir".
